vocabulary.meaning_en: a group of words without both a subject and a verb (a black cat, pick up)
a group of words with a subject and a verb
vocabulary.example: "When I got home" is a clause.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a part of a sentence, not a full sentence
vocabulary.example: "Pick up" alone is a sentence fragment.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a clause that makes sense alone; also called the main clause
vocabulary.example: "I ate dinner" is an independent clause.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a clause that needs the main clause to make full sense
vocabulary.example: "When I got home" is a dependent clause.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the independent clause; it has the important information
vocabulary.example: The main clause tells us the key information.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a dependent clause that starts with when, after, before, while...
vocabulary.example: "After I finished work" is a time clause.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a two- or three-word verb (pick up, move out, show off)
to leave your home and live somewhere else
to try to make people notice how good you are
vocabulary.example: He likes to show off his new phone.

vocabulary.meaning_en: able to stand alone; not needing others
vocabulary.example: She is independent; she has her own job and home.
There is something peculiar about this sentence.

fine_lines.title: phrase vs clause
fine_lines.explanation_ar: العبارة (phrase) جزء من جملة فيه فعل أو اسم لكن ليس الاثنين معًا (pick up / a black cat). الجملة (clause) فيها فاعل وفعل (I got home). جيمس يشبّه العبارة بباتمان (مفيدة بلا قوى خارقة) والجملة بسوبرمان (أقوى).
fine_lines.explanation_en: A phrase is a sentence fragment with a verb or a noun, but not both (pick up / a black cat). A clause has a subject and a verb (I got home). James calls the phrase Batman (useful, no superpowers) and the clause Superman (more powerful).

examples.sentence: when I got home / I ate dinner

fine_lines.title: independent vs dependent clause
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المستقلة تُفهم وحدها (I ate dinner). التابعة لا تكتمل وحدها وتجعلك تنتظر البقية (When I got home...).
fine_lines.explanation_en: An independent clause makes sense alone (I ate dinner). A dependent clause doesn't finish the idea; you wait for more (When I got home...).

expressions.phrase: When I got home, I ate dinner.
expressions.meaning_ar: عندما وصلتُ إلى البيت تناولتُ العشاء.
expressions.meaning_en: Dependent clause first, so use a comma.
expressions.example: When I got home, I ate dinner.

expressions.phrase: I ate dinner when I got home.
expressions.meaning_ar: تناولتُ العشاء عندما وصلتُ إلى البيت.
expressions.meaning_en: Main clause first, so no comma.
expressions.example: I ate dinner when I got home.
We're out of time. Let me wrap it up.
Native speakers talk fast. Get used to it.

grammar.title: Phrase: verb OR noun, not both
grammar.explanation_ar: العبارة جزء من جملة فيها فعل أو اسم فقط، بدون فاعل + فعل. مثل الأفعال المركّبة (pick up, move out) أو مجموعة اسمية (a black cat).
grammar.explanation_en: A phrase is a sentence fragment with a verb or a noun only, no subject + verb. For example, phrasal verbs (pick up, move out) or a noun group (a black cat).

grammar.title: Clause: subject + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: الجملة (clause) فيها فاعل وفعل. الجمل المركبة فيها جزءان: جملة مستقلة (رئيسية) وجملة تابعة (زمنية أو وصفية أو ظرفية).
grammar.explanation_en: A clause has a subject and a verb. Complex sentences have two parts: an independent (main) clause and a dependent clause (time, adjective or adverb clause).

grammar.title: Comma rule for clause order
grammar.explanation_ar: إذا جاءت الجملة التابعة أولًا نضع فاصلة بعدها. إذا جاءت الجملة الرئيسية أولًا فلا نضع فاصلة.
grammar.explanation_en: If the dependent clause comes first, put a comma after it. If the main clause comes first, no comma.
examples: When I got home, I ate dinner.
I ate dinner when I got home.

grammar.title: Four time-clause words: when, after, before, while
grammar.explanation_ar: هذه الكلمات تبدأ الجملة الزمنية في الماضي، وتُستخدم أيضًا للمستقبل.
grammar.explanation_en: These words start time clauses in the past; they are also used for the future.
examples: After I finished work, I went home.
Before I left, I locked the door.
While I was cooking, the phone rang.
When I arrive, I will call you.

questions.question: In "When I got home, I ate dinner", the independent clause is ___.
Choose the correct punctuation.
choices: I ate dinner, when I got home.
When I got home I, ate dinner.
When, I got home I ate dinner.
When I got home, I ate dinner.
questions.explanation_en: Dependent clause first → comma after it.

questions.question: "I ate dinner when I got home." Do we need a comma?
choices: No, the main clause comes first.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the four time-clause words in the lesson?
questions.explanation_ar: الكلمات الأربع: when, after, before, while.
questions.explanation_en: The four words: when, after, before, while.

questions.question: Another name for the independent clause is the ___.
"Show off" is a ___.
questions.explanation_en: A phrasal verb with no subject: a phrase.

questions.question: "___ I was cooking, the phone rang."
